title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_f0f
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy group compromise using the Fysbis backdoor on a Linux system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident. The Fysbis backdoor is a modular Linux trojan/backdoor that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of Executable and Linking Format (ELF) binaries. Fysbis can install itself to a victim system with or without root privileges.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can SSH into the `next-target` host using the same credentials. Enter `start` to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can SSH into the `next-target` host using the same credentials. Enter `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the `target` host and identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service: systemkernelservicedefender.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl status systemkernelservicedefender.service` to inspect the suspicious service.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service identified in the previous task is automatically started after a reboot.
levels.solution: Examine the systemd service files and timers to see how the service is configured to start automatically. The hidden flag is the name of the systemd service or persistence identifier: systemkernelservicedefender.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd service files and timers to see how the service is configured to start automatically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` to list all service files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service` to inspect the service file.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Process
levels.content: Identify the process responsible for the suspicious activity on the `target` host.
levels.solution: Use process monitoring tools to identify any unusual processes and their associated network connections. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious process: ncat.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use process monitoring tools to identify any unusual processes and their associated network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ps aux` to list all running processes.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run `netstat -tulnp | grep ncat` to check network connections related to the suspicious process.
